answer: Latency-chained attestation. Each agent's reply must include a fresh random pulse echoed from the requester's prior message, signed and logged on a shared ridge of timestamped hashes that any node can recheck. Because every attestation reuses the exact challenge nonce, an attacker cannot copy a valid answer to a second identity, and the ledger's terrace ordering exposes duplicates within one window. Replaying or farming N identities costs N distinct signed round-trips plus the compute to win each timing slot, so forgery scales linearly with real work rather than identity count.
